note: The required-suite manifest. Every entry must produce a JUnit report whenever its module is in the gate's scope. A suite that is renamed, deleted, or emptied without a deliberate decision here FAILS the no-hidden-skips gate. minTests is a floor taken from the phase report that introduced the suite, not from the current count: it is the last number a human reviewed, so a suite that loses tests needs a decision, not a smaller number.
nestedSuiteNote: A JUnit @Nested suite is reported under its @DisplayName, not its class name: the XML file is TEST-...NonHttpBoundaryTest$AiTools.xml but testsuite/@name is 'AI tool execution is application-owned and deny-by-default'. The no-hidden-skips checker and every waiver therefore have to address such a suite by its REPORTED name. `suite` keeps the class name for traceability; `reportName` is what appears in a report and in a waiver. RECOMMENDATION for the security/worker owners: give every @Nested class an explicit, stable id so the reported name cannot drift with copy-editing.
containerClassNote: A test class whose tests are ALL inside @Nested classes is NOT registered here, and that is deliberate. Six such container entries were removed on 2026-10-07 (ExportJobLifecycleIntegrationTest, ExportCatalogueCapabilityIntegrationTest, AdminAuditStreamIntegrationTest, ConnectorAndSearchOperationsIntegrationTest, FinancePeriodLifecycleIntegrationTest, AiRunChildScopeBackfillIntegrationTest). Registering one required a report JUnit does not reliably emit: ExportJobLifecycleIntegrationTest produced its own XML when run alone and NOT when the whole module ran, so a green build failed for a non-event. A flaky assertion trains people to delete manifest entries to get a green gate, which is the exact failure this gate exists to prevent. The protection is not lost. Each container's assertions live in its nested suites, all registered with real floors totalling 128 tests, and because those entries are named Container$Nested, deleting or renaming the container makes them fail as REQUIRED SUITE MISSING. The outer entry added nothing they did not already guarantee.

Phase 14 (ADR-0014, CX-1): capacity regression - six projects AND six organizations each take a first customer reference; strict monotonicity; no reuse after deletion; concurrent writers get different references; cross-tenant negatives

Asks the running application for its own OpenAPI document and writes it to build/openapi for promotion to tests/contracts/openapi.json. No database: it describes the web layer and must never stamp or migrate one. check-openapi-document.ps1 compares the committed contract against this output.

ADR-0016. Every declared success code is an OBSERVED one, the refusals are derived per operation rather than pasted on, and an operation cannot declare a code it never returns or omit one it does. The observed table lives in shared-kernel, NOT in the customiser, so the document is stamped FROM the table and a document edited to match a route cannot pass this.

suites.reportName: an unauthenticated provider POST is admitted on its signature
suites.note: Phase 36. A correctly signed Meta/Telegram POST with no cookie is admitted and durably queued (outbox + idempotency rows asserted, not just a 200). Before Phase 36 it answered 403 CSRF then 401: every inbound provider message was being rejected, and no HTTP test had ever exercised the path.

suites.reportName: an unauthenticated request without a valid signature is refused
suites.note: Phase 36. Absent, malformed, tampered and wrong-secret signatures are all refused, and nothing is queued. This is the half that must not regress: permitAll removes the SESSION requirement, never the AUTHENTICATION requirement.

suites.reportName: the exemption is scoped to /webhooks/** and nothing else
suites.note: Phase 36. /api/v1/** still requires a session after the exemption, and a refusal body names neither the secret, the payload, nor the reason. An exemption that widened past the webhook prefix would be a new incident, not a fix.

suites.reportName: every /webhooks/** route carries the same treatment
suites.note: Phase 36. Enumerates the webhook routes so a route added next month without signature verification fails the gate rather than shipping as an open write path. The unsigned Mock endpoint is gated per request, not only at startup: assertSafeFor refuses to BOOT a production profile, which does not stop the route existing on staging or a demo.

ADR-0016. The one genuine split outcome: an APPLIED replay leaves the row PENDING and claimable, so 202; a REFUSED replay writes nothing and completed on the request, so 200. Both are declared and both are observed over HTTP, which is why this operation declares two success codes.
ADR-0016. POST /api/v1/exports and its retry answer 202 and assert the job row is QUEUED with a null artefact, so the status is proved against state rather than against the response body.

Phase 38. The role vocabulary has to exist in THREE places at once: the Prisma enum, the Flyway chain, and UserRole. fromValue THROWS on an unknown label rather than defaulting, so a users row carrying a role the Java enum omits cannot be read at all -- the user gets a failed sign-in, not a denied action. This asserts the chain against the enum in both directions, that CLINIC_STAFF resolves to a real grant rather than Set.of(), and that it is a strict subset of EMPLOYEE. Red-to-green demonstrated: neutralising the matrix entry turns 2 of the 5 red.

suites.reportName: the clinic read model
suites.note: Phase 37. The clinic read model, which is the FIRST counterpart in the new stack: the legacy runtime has a clinic controller and the Spring backend had no clinic or analytics module at all, so those journeys were not comparable and the strangler could not advance past them.

suites.reportName: every metric carries the rows it was computed from
suites.note: Phase 37. The requirement that decides whether analytics is worth merging: every metric publishes sourceTable, window, derivation, sourceRowIds and a drillThroughPath, and the fixture RE-DERIVES the population with independent SQL, so a wrong derivation fails even when the number happens to be right. An aggregate nobody can trace to rows is a number no finance owner can defend.

suites.reportName: a tenant-A actor receives nothing of tenant B
suites.note: Phase 37. Negative tests, not just positive ones. The lesson carried from the legacy breach is that a scope taken from the client is a REQUEST, not authorization -- so every route is checked with a project or tenant named in the query and in the body, which is exactly how the legacy PermissionsGuard was defeated.

suites.reportName: role refusals
suites.note: Phase 37. Uniform 404 refusals, so a probe cannot distinguish no-such-record from not-yours. Matches the Phase-33 shape.

Phase 37 container marker. Every test lives in the two nested suites registered below, which carry floors of 3+4=7. Declared with containerOf and minTests 0 because its own report appears or does not depending on how JUnit scheduled the class; requiring it would fail a green build for a non-event. check 3c forbids a nested suite of this container from going unfloored.

suites.reportName: every route answers the status it is observed to answer
suites.note: ADR-0016 for the clinic routes: the declared success status is the OBSERVED one. A document edited to match a route would make a bug contractual, which is the failure mode ADR-0016 exists to prevent.

suites.reportName: declarations
suites.note: Phase 37. The refusals each clinic operation can actually produce, derived rather than pasted on: declaring a refusal a route cannot produce is the same lie in the other direction.

Phase 37 container marker. Every test lives in the three nested suites registered below, which carry floors of 3+4+4=11. Container for the same reason as ClinicContractHttpIntegrationTest: its own report is not reliably emitted.

suites.reportName: declared success status

suites.reportName: declared refusals
suites.note: ADR-0016, the refusal direction: a list route declares exactly 401 and 403 and an addressed route exactly 400, 401, 403 and 404 -- asserted as exact sets, so a speculative paste AND an omission both fail.

suites.reportName: the published schemas

suites.reportName: the conversation mode decides whether a run happens
suites.note: Phase 46. The conversation mode decides whether an AI turn happens at all; HUMAN mode and a project with no enabled agent both produce no run.

suites.reportName: exactly one run per inbound message
suites.note: Phase 46. Redelivery is arbitrated by a tenant-scoped unique row, so one inbound message yields one run and one charge.

suites.reportName: a draft is a draft: nothing is sent
suites.note: Phase 46. The ruling: the orchestrator decides and records, a human sends. No messages row, no outbound-send intent, no workflow_runs row.

suites.reportName: a human takeover withholds the draft
suites.note: Phase 46. Takeover before and after the answer both withhold the draft, so an AI turn cannot land on a conversation a human owns.

suites.reportName: a policy refusal is an outcome, not an exception

suites.reportName: the handler's own refusals

suites.reportName: the route answers what it is observed to answer

suites.reportName: the batched projections are the per-row projections
suites.note: Phase 48. GET /api/v1/customers issued 1 + 3 x 50 = 151 statements, every one correct and index-served and every one individually fast. These assert the batched page projection is the SAME projection: same latestTicket, same five leads in the same order, same five appointments, a customer with no conversation still null rather than blank, an unreachable project yields nothing, another tenant's id is absent from the batch rather than merely its ticket, and an empty page asks for nothing rather than asking `in ()` which PostgreSQL rejects.

suites.reportName: a page is read once, not once per row
suites.note: Phase 48, and the assertion that makes the fix load-bearing without depending on wall-clock: a 50-row page calls the batched reader once and the per-row reader zero times, and the statement count is the same for a 5-row page as for a 50-row page. Red-to-green proven by reverting loadPageProjection to the per-row loop: exactly these three statement-count tests went red while the equivalence tests stayed green.
